raw_response:
I am not farming big land, only 14 mu, and at my age I do what is steady and what I know. Wheat and maize are still my backbone because they feed the family and bring regular money, so I keep 8 mu in wheat-maize. Cotton I still plant on 4 mu because I know how to manage it and it spreads the risk. Chili I keep only 2 mu, not too much, because it needs more hand work and watching. With only 3 people in the house and some going out for work, I cannot make everything labor-heavy. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I water at the key times, not too often. For fertilizer, I do like I always do, not too little because I am afraid yield will fall, but not too much either because cash is tight. If the crop looks weak, I add a little more. Seed I buy from the local market, mostly what people around here use.

For wheat, I plant in October after clearing the land, use ordinary local seed, put base fertilizer before sowing, then add urea once when it starts standing up in spring. Wheat needs water, so I plan a few irrigations if rain is not enough. After wheat harvest in June, I do not waste time because maize must go in quickly. Usually I just clear the straw, do light tillage or rotary tilling, and sow maize right away. Cotton and chili are on their own plots. Cotton is slower but familiar, and chili can sell for better money if the market is good, though it needs more labor for transplanting, picking, and spraying. I keep chili area small for that reason.
